keyFindings.description: The only thing standing at this head, and one string. The test is named "dispatch_issue_update takes the four priority buckets and null, and moves by neighbour, never by a rank field", but its body (:554-566) asserts the four priority buckets, their refusals, and that `{ issue, rank: "a0" }` is refused under strict — nothing in it exercises `before`/`after` acceptance, which lives in the accepted-rows test at :468-473. The cost is concrete: someone pruning those rows leaves a suite that still claims "moves by neighbour" and no longer checks it. Name it for what it asserts and leave the reasoning to the comment at :549-552, which is already accurate. Round 1 left this on the Fast-follow line; the architect ruled it is not deferred, so it is this round's finding.

roundOneFindingsAnswered.evidence: The line now reads "A closed issue takes only a board move (`--before` / `--after`), `components`, a reopening status, and an external-links write that adds no link.", matching the tool description at packages/contracts/src/dispatch-tools.ts:417-419 and the server's own rule at packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/issue_patch.go:202-216. No text under skills/ or docs/ names `rank` as a field an agent sets.

The spec's example is now `{ issue: "DSP-1", priority: 1, before: "DSP-2" }` — the move riding along with another change, which is the shape the tool's own text promises. It is schema-valid under the assertion that covers every example (packages/contracts/src/dispatch-tools.test.ts:298) and survives render-then-parse (packages/envoy-client/src/__tests__/dispatch-command.test.ts:49-54). The three committed claude-envoy bundles carry it.

`await run({ before: "" })` now asserts the PATCH carries `rank: { before: "" }`, with the reason in a comment: the tool sends the empty value so the server answers `rank neighbor must name another issue` (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/issue_rank.go), and a falsy or trimming guard would drop the key and turn that refusal into a silent no-move.

declined.description: The deep-review pass rated it a Low finding that the new example shows a board move on every `issue-update` refusal while a refusal prints no description (packages/envoy-client/src/tool-input-errors.ts:16-30), so the keeper caveat at :424-425 reaches only `--help` readers, and skills/dispatch/references/issues.md:12 tells most agents never to reorder. Not asked for: its remediation (an example that stays off the board) undoes round 1's finding, since packages/contracts/AGENTS.md:62 exists so the example shows the argument shape, and its alternative (the caveat on the argument descriptions) reaches only the surface that already carries it. Recorded on the pull request's Not proven / risk line as a stated residue instead. The code-quality pass weighed the same swap and requested no change.

The code-quality pass asked that the printed move read `rank.after`/`rank.before` rather than the locals, and that the deliberate top-down inversion be stated in the comment at :2883-2884. Declined: the locals and the sent object are built from the same two values eleven lines apart with nothing between them that can diverge, the inversion is pinned by the executor test's expected text, and the README documents the printed form (packages/envoy-client/README.md:360-362).

Round 1's declined narrowing of `IssueRankInput` stands declined: it is the shared Dispatch wire shape generated into Go and read by the server, and the executor is its only producer, guarded on `undefined` rather than falsiness and locked by two assertions.
